question: In which among the following years was Hindu widow remarriage declared legal in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1856**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act, 1856 was enacted on 26 July 1856.
 
• The Act was formulated to legalize the remarriage of Hindu widows in India.
 
• This legislation was a significant social reform during British rule in India.
 
• It was largely advocated by social reformers such as Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar.
 
• The Act aimed to improve the condition of Hindu widows who were traditionally not allowed to remarry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar:**

 
 
• He was a prominent Indian educator and social reformer.
 
• He played a crucial role in the enactment of the Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act, 1856.
 
• His efforts were pivotal in challenging orthodox Hindu society and promoting widow remarriage.
 
 
 
• **The Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act, 1856:**
 
 
• The Act provided legal safeguards and rights to widows who chose to remarry.
 
• It also annulled the stigma and social ostracism faced by widows for remarrying.
 
 
 
• **Social Impact:**
 
 
• The enactment of the Act marked a progressive step towards the modernization of Indian society.
 
• It laid the foundation for further social reforms concerning women's rights in India.
 
 
 
• **British India's Social Reforms:**
 
 
• The 19th century saw several social reforms initiated under British rule, addressing various social issues.
 
• These reforms included the abolition of Sati and the promotion of education among women.
